summary: IDP attribute delimiter change causes orgUnit claim mismatch and RBAC resolution failures for internal tools
description: Issue summary: After a planned IDP attribute release on 2026-03-09, some users receive an 'organizationUnit' claim using a pipe (|) delimiter instead of the expected colon (:) delimiter. Impact: token-to-role mapping in the RBAC service fails to match these altered claims, resulting in 403s when accessing internal tools (feature-flag console, runbook editor, and analytics portal). Current behavior: tokens present correctly but role resolution returns empty set when the orgUnit claim contains the pipe delimiter. Expected behavior: RBAC claim parser should accept either delimiter (legacy colon or new pipe) or the IDP should continue emitting the colon-delimited value. Workaround (temporary): Manual role grant to affected accounts via the admin console until a fix is deployed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Authenticate via Okta/IDP for a user with orgUnit attribute set to 'engineering|backend'
2) Request access to /console or /runbooks with the issued session token
3) Observe 403 from RBAC service and 'no roles resolved' in token resolution trace
4) Compare token claim payloads between a working user (engineering:backend) and failing user (engineering|backend)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Lionel Chen: Reported via #internal-auth — several engineers hitting 403 for console after login. Not widespread but reproducible for new hires in 'backend' sub-org.
2026-03-10 09:45 - Asha Patel: Confirmed token claim uses '|' delimiter. Opening this ticket and assigning to auth+platform to triage. Adding SRE for traffic patterns.
2026-03-11 14:03 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Observed spike in 'role_resolution_failure' metric correlated with IDP deploy window. Temporary mitigation suggested: admin-grant for affected accounts.

2026-03-12 08:55 - Asha Patel: Implemented and tested claim-parser update to accept both ':' and '|' locally. Preparing patch for staging and coordinating with IDP team to revert emission format if needed.
investigation: Hypothesis: IDP provisioning change introduced a new delimiter for composite orgUnit values. RBAC regex expects '(.+):(.+)' and fails on '|'.
Checked token traces for ~12 affected users; all show consistent '|' in orgUnit. Legacy users provisioned before 2026-03-09 continue to have ':' and work normally.
Confirmed IDP release notes (internal) mention change to 'composite attribute separator' to support downstream systems, but RBAC was not included in scope.
Ran local unit tests: updated parser to accept /[:|]/ and role resolution succeeds with both separators.
Risk assessment: broad rollout of parser change is low-risk but we must ensure no accidental collision with existing role naming conventions that use '|' in other contexts.
resolution: 2026-03-12 16:30 - Rollout plan: stage patch to identity-proxy and rbac-service that accepts both ':' and '|' delimiters in orgUnit claim parser. Patch referenced in PR #7251.
2026-03-12 17:10 - Coordinated with IDP team to temporarily revert attribute emission to ':' for new provisioning windows while patch deploys to staging.
2026-03-13 02:00 - Deploy to prod scheduled during low-traffic window; monitoring dashboard alerts established for 'role_resolution_failure' and error budget impact.
Follow-up: Add an integration test that validates claim delimiter variants and add IDP to the onboarding checklist for RBAC impact review on attribute changes.
notes: Owner: auth-platform team to complete patch and monitor for 48 hours post-deploy.
If further delimiter variants appear, pivot to a canonical claim transformation step at the identity-proxy boundary to normalize values.
Add a short postmortem if rollback or unexpected regressions occur.
